subject: Banking
title: Wise: Killing Bank FX Margins
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Wise: Killing Bank FX Margins.

hook.text: Wise charges 0.5-1% for international transfers. Banks charge 3-5% hidden in the exchange rate. Wise exposes the markup.

buildup.text: Banks profit from opaque exchange rates. They quote a rate 3-5% worse than mid-market and call it 'free transfer.'

discovery.text: Wise shows the real exchange rate and charges a transparent flat fee.

twist.text: Wise processes $12 billion monthly. It's profitable, publicly traded.

climax.text: Wise won by being transparent in an industry built on hidden fees.

punchline.text: 0.5% vs. 3-5%. Wise wins by showing what banks hide in the exchange rate.

quiz.question: How do banks hide international transfer profits?
options: By marking up the exchange rate 3-5% above mid-market

details.summary: Wise, formerly TransferWise, disrupted international money transfers by offering the real exchange rate with transparent fees, exposing how traditional banks had been hiding massive markups inside unfavorable exchange rates.
details.whyItMatters: Banks were charging hidden markups of 3 to 5 percent on international transfers, costing global consumers and businesses billions. Wise's transparency forced banks to reduce margins on cross-border payments.
takeaways: Wise uses the mid-market exchange rate with a small transparent fee
Traditional banks typically mark up exchange rates by 3 to 5 percent
Wise processes over $100 billion annually in cross-border transfers

faq.question: How does Wise offer better exchange rates than banks?
faq.answer: Wise uses a peer-to-peer matching system where possible, pairing customers sending money in opposite directions. When direct matching is not possible, it uses the mid-market rate and charges a transparent fee rather than hiding margins in the exchange rate.

faq.question: How much do hidden bank FX markups cost consumers?
faq.answer: A bank claiming zero fees on an international transfer might apply a 3% markup on the exchange rate. On a $10,000 transfer, that hidden fee is $300. Wise would charge around $50 for the same transfer, saving the customer $250.
